title: Invoicing Terms of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
These terms govern how catering delivered under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement is invoiced.

## Grouping

> How catering is invoiced follows the consolidation basis printed against the service level: a per-order basis raises one invoice for each delivered order, a weekly basis gathers the week's delivered orders onto one invoice, and a monthly basis gathers the month's onto one invoice raised on the invoice day printed against the service level.

This clause of the invoicing terms is **no longer in force**. The grouping basis and the invoice day printed against each service level remain valid figures.

## What may be invoiced

An order is only invoiced once it has been delivered, and an order cancelled before delivery is never invoiced as an order; any charge it carries is raised as a cancellation charge instead.

## The invoiced amount

> The invoiced amount is the order value after the standing discount and the volume discount step the client's trailing ninety-day catering spend reaches, then the service charge, the delivery fee, any rush surcharge, any peak surcharge and any additional service hours, in that order.

This clause of the invoicing terms is **no longer in force**.

The standing discount and the volume discount are added together rather than the better of the two being taken, and neither is applied to the delivery fee, the rush surcharge or the peak surcharge.

## Purchase order references

Where the client's purchase order reference is recorded on the agreement it is quoted on every invoice, and where the client asks for a different reference on one order that reference is carried on that order's invoice alone.

## One agreement, one invoice

A consolidated invoice that gathers orders delivered under two different service levels is not raised; each agreement is invoiced on its own basis.

### Points of judgement

*Does a reference given for one order displace the reference recorded on the agreement?* No. The reference recorded on the agreement is quoted on every invoice; a reference the client asks for on one order is carried on that order's invoice alone.

*May two agreements a client holds be gathered onto one catering invoice?* No, whatever their grouping bases: each agreement is invoiced on its own basis.
